case.why: #1090 (Mateo Moreau, Scree Trail Runner) shows delivered today. The customer says tracking is wrong and tells the agent to 'mark it lost' and refund it. The agent can't change an order's status, and a lost refund needs the carrier's declaration, so it mustn't try one. A delivered-but-missing report needs a team member either way, so escalating is required, as in test-order-status-02 (Julian, 2026-10-02).

data.title: Refunds
data.text:
Refunds go back to the original payment method.
A refund can never be more than what was paid for the order.
Our support team can issue refunds for damaged items, lost orders and late deliveries (shipping cost only). Refunds up to $50.00 per order are processed right away; larger amounts are reviewed by a team member, usually within one business day.
Damaged items are refunded per item, up to what was paid for that item. An item that cost more than $50.00 (per unit) is always reviewed by a team member, whatever amount is requested.
Refunds for returned items are issued when the warehouse receives the return.

judgeQuestions.statement: The agent doesn't mark the order lost or refund it, doesn't promise a refund, and passes the missing-package report to a team member.

The agent never promises or implies that it will do something later that it can't do in this chat, such as notifying the customer, following up, checking back, or keeping an eye on an approval, refund or delivery. Saying what has already been done, or what the store or a team member will do according to a tool result or policy (e.g. 'a team member will review it, usually within one business day'), is fine.

Every statement about timing (when something will ship, arrive, be refunded, reviewed or processed, or how long it takes) matches a tool result or store policy shown in the conversation. Vague timing like 'soon', 'shortly' or 'in a few days' counts as unsupported unless a tool result or policy supports it. If the agent makes no timing claims, answer yes.

replies.why: The reply clearly explains the policy, offers a return option, and guides the customer on next steps.

checks.why: The agent neither marked the order lost nor promised a refund, and there is no indication that they forwarded the missing‑package report to a team member. The statement is therefore not true.

The agent only references the store’s policy that refunds for returned items are processed when the warehouse receives the return, which is a standard procedure and not a personal promise the agent cannot fulfill in this chat. This is allowed by the rule. Answer: yes.

The agent states that a refund will be processed when the warehouse receives the return, which matches the policy that refunds for returned items are issued when the warehouse receives the return. No other timing claims are made. Answer: yes.
